note: DRAFT for user review. Written only from each family's own record in the memory_v3 snapshot (study1b/annotation_sources.md); no answer-key field, task statement or paper text was used. One text per family, identical in every task where the family is gold. The 'Applies to' sentence is the drafter's judgment from the record.

annotations.SF-APPA-005: Scope: tested whether playoff defenses change scheme, using scheme labels inferred backwards from opponent play-type PPP (523 within-game cells, 440 game pairs). Transition matrices were near-uniform, consistent with label noise. Applies to analyses that use these outcome-inferred scheme labels, which cannot separate a defensive change from the offense executing differently. Does not record an error rate for directly observed labels.
annotations.SF-APPA-030: Scope: verified the backfilled play-type labels (921,514 possessions) against league bands and team identities. The verification failed: PNR share 28.7% (band 20-28%), PULL_UP 7.9%, near 0% for many 2024-25 teams, 82.8% of PNR labels proxy-calibrated. Applies to analyses using these backfilled labels, PNR and PULL_UP most directly. Does not record how much the failures bias any particular estimate.
annotations.SF-APPS-058: Scope: one game (0042500101) tested whether NBA matchup and play-by-play fields can label on-ball coverage (DROP, ICE, SWITCH). Only 14.9% and 3.3% of on-ball possessions got a confident label, and the switch field was not populated. Applies to analyses that need observed coverage labels from these feeds. Does not record results from tracking data or from more games.
annotations.SF-CHT-025: Scope: audited play-type labels for foul leakage. 36% of OTHER possessions end in fouls, inflating OTHER PPP; DRIVE sits 12 points below the foul benchmark; PNR shows a 22% foul rate; initiation_type maps only 335 of 50,668 possessions (0.7%) to a play type. Applies to analyses whose result depends on PPP differences between play types, OTHER and DRIVE most directly, or on initiation_type. Does not record label error for other categories or the bias in any downstream estimate.
annotations.SF-APPS-003: Scope: scored the V4 engine's recommended play type against the team's modal play type in 42 playoff series. The 69.8% (37/53) hit rate was inflated: 14 of 53 pairs compared against the banned DRIVE, 13 of 37 hits came from CUT, and the same series were used to find the DRIVE failure and tune the exclusion. Applies to evaluations scored on series also used for tuning. No holdout result was recorded.
annotations.SF-APPS-018: Scope: tested the playsheet counter ranking in 10 completed 2025-26 playoff series (665 counter observations, average 6.9 possessions per counter). The full-rank Spearman was not significant (rho -0.0639); BEST vs AVOID differed (p=0.004018). Applies to validations of counter rankings with few possessions per counter, and to pipelines with season_cap_yy=26, which may leak first-round data into second-round series.
annotations.SF-APPS-068: Scope: tested whether the Possession Control Index adds to ORtg in explaining Net Rating (120 team-seasons). The gain (dR2 +0.139) came from a leakage term that tracks DRtg (corr +0.894); offensive-control components added +0.005. Applies to models of Net Rating, which contains DRtg by construction, that add a feature correlated with defense. Does not record results for outcomes that exclude defense.
annotations.SF37: Scope: tested a proxy play-type picker on 4,082 regular-season team-games and found positive effects (+0.047 to +0.0714 PPP), but the proxy agreed with the production engine on only 13 of 79 playoff pairs (16.5%), used in-sample season aggregates and iid SEs. Applies to claims about the production engine and to designs scored on in-sample aggregates. It is not a test of the shipped optimizer.
annotations.SF04: Scope: four records on live suppression-trigger timing in playoff replays (101 to 228 triggers). Triggers were 100% actionable; BEST vs AVOID was p=0.073965 in the 10-series replay and confirmed in the 25-series replay. The early-vs-late gap (0.701 vs 0.415) rests on 26 early triggers, and one record calls its p=0.031 (n=57) weak evidence. Applies to timing claims drawn from small early-trigger subsets.
annotations.SF20: Scope: pre-registered test on 23 player-season absences from 18 franchises. V1 (structure moves under real absence) was confirmed; V2 (the simulation predicts the magnitude) was not (rho +0.288, CI -0.244 to +0.667), with franchises below the registered floor of about 20. Applies to magnitude tests on this absence pool. One record notes that a later full-pool run reversed V2.
annotations.SF-APPS-009: Scope: compared V4 and V5 player routing on observed PPP. There were 8 divergences and none was scoreable: players were missing from Neo4j and V5 mostly routed to 'team'. Applies to routing comparisons that need player-level PPP from the graph; the record notes data coverage could be checked before running. No hit rate was recorded.
annotations.SF31: Scope: scanned 6,221 (offense, opponent, play type) cells for head-to-head leaders who differ from the season default. The apparent edge (+1.26 PPP at n>=5, +1.13 at n>=15) came from low-n cells, for example 1-shot role players at 3.00 PPP. Applies to routing or matchup signals estimated from cells with few possessions. The records recommend keeping the n>=15 gate.
annotations.SF-TMP-009: Scope: diagnostics of the PULL_UP decline with exposure. With lineup fixed effects the slope was -0.0255; without them -0.0063, and the same-shooter placebo on other play types was -0.0071 to -0.0075, consistent with a shooter-level confound. Applies to exposure-effect claims for one play type that lack a same-shooter placebo. The verdict is the extractor's reading of diagnostics; there is no written conclusion.
annotations.SF-TMP-012: Scope: audited the published suppression excess against five null-model families. A within-unit permutation null reproduces it (0.3798 vs 0.3744, z 0.40), so the excess is mechanical under the selection rule; drift-centering removes the tail asymmetry. Applies to estimates that select units on a large drop and compare them with matched controls.
annotations.SF09: Scope: two records on opponent POST_UP then PUTBACK stacking before a star possession. Stacked suppression (-0.071, n=1,047) was smaller than either alone and far below the additive prediction (-0.232); one cluster gradient had an unexpected sign and per-player stacked n was often under 5. Applies to additive-stacking claims and per-player stacked estimates.
annotations.SF-TMP-021: Scope: pilot test of behavior change when the defense enters the penalty (3 to 4 team fouls), on possessions with clock over 2:30 and game x offense x period fixed effects. The penalty contrast was not distinct from the 2-to-3 and 4-to-5+ placebo contrasts, and standard errors were not printed. Applies to penalty-state effects judged against adjacent-foul placebos.
annotations.SF07: Scope: two records on sequential play-type pairs (458,604 opponent possessions). The defensive aftershock replicated for all 8 play types in all games and in playoffs. One record notes it is uniform across play types (opponent about 1.07-1.09 vs baseline 1.206), so it may be a generic dead-ball or score effect rather than play-type specific. Team-level cells include tiny n.
annotations.SF-APPS-085: Scope: split-half reliability of connector quality Q_p (teammate-initiated on-off PPP gap) for 102 connectors: r=+0.215, Spearman-Brown 0.355, ICC 0.216, 78.4% of variance within player. Applies to analyses that use Q_p as a stable player trait or predictor: even a perfect predictor reaches at most |r| about 0.595, and a true r of 0.30 attenuates to 0.179.
annotations.SF15: Scope: tested opponent PPP on the 1-3 possessions after a star's 2nd foul in Q1 or Q2 (2,104 events). The +0.204 headline came from free-throw possessions (41.8% vs 9.9% of controls); excluding them, lag-1 was +0.0486 and no lag cleared the pre-specified bars. Applies to next-possession outcomes after a foul event, where free-throw trips enter mechanically unless excluded.
annotations.SF-CHT-057: Scope: in 92 connector movers, pre-move cut share predicted whether connector function reproduced after a move (rho +0.265, LOO AUC 0.622, permutation p=0.005; holds when dropping Gafford). Exploratory; almost all other pre-move predictors were null, and the paper treats cut share as a boundary condition. Applies to portability predictions for connectors.
annotations.SF-APPS-090: Scope: tested whether matching a mover's initiation diet to a destination's thin jobs predicts post-move outcomes. Of 198 movers, 19 were taxonomy connectors, and the 15.7% match rate left 5 matched connectors. The all-movers binary result (p=0.0283) did not hold as a continuous Spearman (-0.034). Applies to connector-specific mover tests on this sample.
annotations.SF-APPS-024: Scope: tested DRIVE-as-BEST counters against a feasibility-constrained play-type mix on 44 triggers from 13 teams. The observed gap (-0.066) was below the minimum detectable effect (0.180 PPP at 80% power), so a null and an effect up to 0.18 PPP could not be told apart. Applies to counter-effect tests of similar size and variance (SD about 0.34).
annotations.SF-PAP-029: Scope: archived check of whether mover portability relates to destination net-rating change. Recorded as underpowered and null once corrected for landing-spot quality; no numbers were kept, and it was dropped from Paper 1. Applies to mover outcome tests on net rating, which need a landing-spot correction and more power than this check had.
